body:
`node_from_json` is currently broken: it calls `term.fetch(...)` on an undefined local variable, and it also doesn’t preserve a stable mapping from symbol names to `FreeTerm` instances. That means repeated occurrences of the same variable (e.g., "a") won’t refer to the same proposition, which invalidates the generated formula and can make satisfiable/equivalence checks meaningless. Fix by using the provided `terms` hash (e.g., `terms[name] ||= FreeTerm.new`).
```suggestion
      name = ary[0]
      term = terms[name] ||= FreeTerm.new
```

-            LogicNode.inc_minisat_sat_solves
+            LogicNode.inc_z3_sat_solves

body: `LogicNode#satisfiable?` now depends on `cfg_arch` (via `ExtensionTerm#to_z3` / `ParameterTerm#to_z3`), but both memoization (`@memo.is_satisfiable`) and the global `@@cache` are keyed only by the node. This can return incorrect results when the same `LogicNode` instance (or same hash) is checked against different `ConfiguredArchitecture`s. It also breaks callers that still invoke `LogicNode#satisfiable?` without `cfg_arch` (e.g., `Udb::AbstractCondition#covered_by?` builds a `LogicNode` and calls `contradiction.satisfiable?` with no args). Consider keying memo/cache by an identifier derived from `cfg_arch` (or removing cross-arch caching) and update call sites accordingly.

body:
through some trial/error/pain, I've discovered that Gemfile.lock files are not as locked as you (I) might think. This command generates slightly different output when the file exists to begin with. I also discovered that in circumstances, "bundle exec" will actually modify your lock file. It has to do with multi-platform support.

What I have here seems to be the magic sauce that keeps everything stable.
